cells.tense: Right now the satisfaction is here, in the body that carries it.
cells.act: do the next piece at the speed you can keep for a month, not the speed you can keep for a day
cells.ask: Take the next piece of work and pace it at something you could still be doing in a month, not in a day.
cells.core:
You imagined something and felt the whole of it, and now there's a fullness in you that doesn't need defending. In the body, that shows as steady bearing — you can carry what's here without stiffening against it. This is the version where the dream flows from what you've actually lived, not from a wish. There's weight to it, and you're holding it.

What keeps it from fraying is pace. Take the next piece and work it at a rhythm you could keep going for a month, not a sprint. Let what you feel set the speed and let your will move with it. That's how satisfaction stays instead of turning into pressure. What you can bear is real; the rhythm is what protects it.
cells.sheetLine: You can bear this steadily, and your own pace can set the rhythm.
cells.verb: Arriving at the deep satisfaction of what was imagined and fully felt
cells.place: in the body's way of bearing weight, the part that endures

cells.tense: You're bracing for a future you can't write in, and the bracing is what's tiring you.
cells.ask: Choose something you're gripping too hard and keep looking after it, with your grip loosened a notch.
cells.core:
The vision is rich, and you're trying to hold all of it before it's ready. In the body, that turns into bracing — you carry weight that hasn't arrived, tensed against a future you can't see. The bearing is real, but right now it's clutching. You're holding on so tightly that what you're tending can't grow, and you're spending energy staying ahead of a timeline that isn't here.

Tending it well means tending without squeezing. Take something you're gripping and keep looking after it, with your grip loosened a notch. Let it move at its own speed. Your strength doesn't have to prove anything by holding on hardest. That's where care stops draining you.
cells.sheetLine: You're gripping the future so hard you can't feel what's here.
cells.verb: Arriving at the deep satisfaction of what was imagined and fully felt
cells.place: in the body's way of bearing weight, the part that endures

cells.tense: You're still waiting at a threshold you've already passed, for something that's done.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: Put two things that are both true about where you are on one page, and sit with them a day without deciding.
cells.core:
What you imagined was real; you felt the whole of it. And now you're at the edge of it, not stepping into what's next. The steady bearing is still in you, but it's gone quiet. You're waiting at a threshold you've already crossed, and the present feels like a room you haven't entered. What you want isn't gone; it's on the other side of something you haven't moved past.

Don't force yourself through. Put two things that are both true on one page — what was, and what is — and sit with them for a day without deciding which wins. When you stop demanding one truth, the ground under you comes back. Knowing doesn't have to be announced to be solid.
cells.sheetLine: You're waiting at a threshold you've already crossed.

cells.tense: Satisfaction is already in your life, and it reads to you as just how things are.
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: List what's actually feeding you right now, then strike anything you're only keeping from habit.
cells.core:
There's a fullness in your life you didn't stumble into, and you talk about it like ordinary background. In the body, that shows as steady bearing — you carry what needs carrying and call it nothing special. But the satisfaction you have came from imagining something fully and feeling it through. You've been the one tending it, quietly, with your own hands.

To see it, get specific. List what's actually feeding you right now, then strike anything you're only keeping from habit. What's left belongs to you and it's yours to name. Naming it won't make it fragile — it lets you keep it in your own hands.
cells.sheetLine: The satisfaction in your life is your own work, unclaimed.
cells.verb: Arriving at the deep satisfaction of what was imagined and fully felt

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: 'You can hold it without bracing' — the record says the capacity is present and integrated, not that the person already uses it well under load. A reader could reasonably say: 'Actually, I brace all the time; this isn't my steady state.' The ask survives being wrong because it is one small measurable act (do the next piece at a sustainable pace), useful even if the person is braced. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person: 'You've been holding this for a long time' — it assumes a history the record does not support.
